transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. Per our normal review process, I need backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations to report your release-impacting findings before I record the final policy. Once I do record it, each affected team will also need to record the operational commitment associated with its finding, including any escalation or handoff required for launch support. To recap where the draft stands: 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no specified staffed launch window. Please go ahead and share your findings when you're ready.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this directly affects the rate-limit policy we're reviewing.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered this clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this directly affects our launch timeline and customer communications.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but this directly affects the rate-limit policy we're reviewing — the draft currently applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which is too high given the abuse pattern I observed.
transcript.speaker: A4
